# t128 yan summary ui

## Description

`user` wants one command that shows what they are working on right now: which tasks
are open, what each one is for, and when it last moved. `yan ls` was meant to be
that and is never used: a flat table that is mostly `done` rows, count columns that
say nothing, and no room for what a task is about. This task replaces it. The
requirement started vague on purpose and is being worked out in conversation, so
this file is where it stands, not a finished spec.

The overview landed on 09-18 (PR #55). The second half, added the same day: `yan ui`, an
HTML work report `user` can show people — what was done and what is left, by date range,
generated from a fixed template with no AI. Its design is accepted; the command is next.

## Deliverables

One list, three marks: `[ ]` to do, `[x]` delivered (with the date), `[-]` decided
against (with the reason).

- [x] 09-18 · PR #54 · `yan ls` is an overview of what is being worked on: a card per
  open task with its title, what it is for, and when it opened, last changed and was
  last active. Open tasks by default, `--status=open|done|all` for the rest.
- [x] 09-18 · PR #53 · Every task records when it was created and when it was closed, to
  the second. Older tasks fall back to the dates in their log.
- [x] 09-18 · PR #53 · The overview shows when a task's code last changed: the newest
  commit or uncommitted edit across the trees it holds. Open tasks only.
- [x] 09-18 · PR #53 · The overview never fails because of the machine it runs on: a
  task whose repository is not cloned here prints `changed unknown`.
- [x] 09-18 · PR #53 · The overview shows when a task's agents last spoke, for all three
  harnesses `user` runs (claude, codex, agy), falling back to the task's log when a
  harness's session file cannot be found.
- [x] 09-18 · PR #54 · `yan show` no longer prints the pane id; it stays in `--json`.
- [x] 09-18 · PR #52 · `brief.md` has a stated shape, a Description and one Deliverables
  list with three marks, written into the three main-agent prompts and seeded by
  `yan task new`.
- [x] 09-18 · The overview's design, accepted by `user`: a card per open task, a one-line
  ledger for finished ones, a matching `yan show` header. Spec `artifacts/uix/design.md`.
- [x] 09-18 · The Herdr end-to-end tests can run twice at once without failing each
  other: agent names carry a per-run suffix.
- [x] 09-18 · PR #51 · `yan abandon` works for a person at a terminal: pick a task, give
  a reason or leave it empty, confirm. The flag form agents use is unchanged.
- [x] 09-18 · PR #50 · A new shift's pane no longer halves the main agent's pane when the
  tab already holds a pane of `user`'s own.
- [x] 09-18 · The design of `yan ui`, accepted by `user`: a work report for people, not
  for yan — what `user` opens when someone asks what they have been doing. One page, no
  sidebar: the date range as the headline with presets `7d · 30d · 90d · 2026 · All` and
  own dates; metrics that follow the range (Finished, In progress, Delivered with bars
  per week, by project); search, state chips and a project picker; a matrix of tasks
  with one square per deliverable, done work first-class and grouped by completion
  month; a row opens into a timeline of its deliverables, left-aligned with the
  description, a date on top of each run. No internal state anywhere: no ids, shifts,
  units, log. Very few words, data rather than labels. Font ChillRoundF (寒蝉圆体) for
  everything, named in the stack and installed by `user`, system font as fallback;
  state icons are a drawn ring filling with the delivered fraction; row dates as grey
  numbers, `09.16 - 09.17`. Spec `artifacts/uix-html/design.md` and `data-shape.md`,
  template `artifacts/uix-html/mock/template.html`, proof `mock/check.mjs`, canvas
  https://claude.ai/artifact/D9LkwBRW8dhB9tyhSj71EZ. Shift s7, six rounds; how it got
  there is in `artifacts/uix-html-round2.md` to `-round6.md` and the log.
- [ ] `yan ui` itself, option A of `artifacts/html-ui-options.md`: the command collects
  every task with no AI, fills the template's one placeholder with a JSON block, writes
  one offline HTML file outside the vault and opens it; `--since/--until` as dates set
  the range the page opens on (`user` says "the past month", yan passes the dates),
  `--json`, `--out`, `--no-open`; `yan ui` added to the three root prompt files. Built
  in three phases, one shift each, plan `artifacts/impl-plan-yan-ui.md`. This also covers the draft's "weekly, monthly report to my boss":
  it is this page with a range, nothing separate.
- [ ] Pending, `user`'s call, not decided: shipping the font in the yan repository
  instead of installing it by hand. ChillRoundF is OFL but 5.9 + 6.7 MB; a per-report
  subset (~50 KB a weight) would need a subsetter dependency. Facts in
  `artifacts/font-research/font-research.md`.
- [-] Rewriting brief Descriptions and deliverables in a voice meant for outside readers
  of the report — `user` on 09-18: the tone does not matter, the page is not handed to

- [-] Units, shifts and tree counts in the overview — `yan show <id>` is where those
  are read; `user` changed their mind on this during the first pass.
- [-] A per-task status word (idle / talking / working) — `user` reads that off the

- [-] A `description` field in `task.json` — the description lives in `brief.md`.
